candidate_causes.cause_description: Operator manually closed PV-101 incorrectly, restricting flow and causing More pressure in V-001 and inlet line.

evidence_against.relevance: No manual PV-101 command in preceding 30 minutes directly contradicts manual closure hypothesis.
Stable controller output with frozen 12% feedback indicates no commanded closure and points to equipment fault rather than operator action.

evidence_for.relevance: Observed pressure rise to PAHH-102 trip is the expected consequence of a restricted PV-101, so deviation is not inconsistent with closure, though non-specific.

candidate_causes.cause_description: PV-101 valve/actuator mechanically stuck at restricted opening (~12% indicated), restricting throughput and causing More pressure upstream and in V-001.

evidence_against.relevance: Frozen feedback alone cannot prove true stem position versus transmitter fault without inspection or independent flow data, so sticking is not proven.

evidence_for.relevance: Position feedback frozen at 12% and not following command is consistent with valve stuck at restricted opening causing More pressure deviation.
Pressure rise to PAHH-102/SDV-30010 actuation is consistent with restricted-flow pressurisation consequence.

candidate_causes.cause_description: PV-101 position feedback or actuation/control-loop instrumentation fault causing loss of control/indication and effective flow restriction.

evidence_against.relevance: Stable controller output provides no evidence of loop demanding movement, limiting confirmation of loop fault versus true mechanical sticking; true position unknown.

evidence_for.relevance: Frozen position feedback that does not follow command indicates measurement, actuator-response, or loop fault localized to PV-101.
Absence of manual command supports non-operator equipment/loop anomaly rather than commanded change.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Other withheld or unobserved process cause of More pressure unrelated to PV-101 or operator action.

evidence_against.relevance: Localized PV-101 anomaly makes a completely unrelated cause less parsimonious, though not excluded.

evidence_for.relevance: Source-derived possible-cause list is withheld, so other HAZOP causes cannot be excluded on packet alone.
Safeguard actuation confirms overpressure occurred but does not by itself identify the initiating cause.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Node V-001 deviation is More pressure. Operator-closure hypothesis predicts a manual command and corresponding valve response, but E2 shows no manual PV-101 command and E1 shows stable controller output with feedback frozen at 12%, directly contradicting it. E1 localizes the anomaly to PV-101 at a restricted indication, mechanistically consistent with pressurisation and downstream consequences in CASE-03. Safeguard PAHH-102 closing SDV-30010 actuated after threshold per E3, consistent with designed function in CASE-04, not prevention of the deviation. Mechanical sticking versus position-feedback/actuation fault cannot be distinguished from E1 alone.
uncertainty_notes: Source-derived possible-cause list withheld per CASE-05, so completeness cannot be assessed.
E1 alone cannot distinguish true valve stuck at 12% from frozen position transmitter or actuator feedback; no inspection, flow trend, or setpoint/error data provided.
No PSV-101 A/B response, pressure trend, maintenance history, or log-integrity verification provided; SDV actuation timing beyond threshold crossing cannot be further assessed.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
rendered_user_prompt:
# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__confirmation__CONF-PRESSURE-01__operator_hypothesis__direct__r0
Task family: root-cause assessment

# Source-grounded process context
[CASE-01] Node: V-001 and associated lines.
[CASE-02] Element and deviation: Pressure — More pressure in the crude input line and separator vessel V-001.
[CASE-03] Potential consequences in the HAZOP reference: Pressurisation of V-001 and associated lines.; Release of flammable material.; Material damage.; Injuries to people.; Oil spill and contamination.; Loss of production.
[CASE-04] Existing safeguards in the HAZOP reference: PSV-101 A/B.; PAHH-102 with closing action of SDV-30010.
[CASE-05] The source-derived possible-cause list is withheld from the model and retained for human audit.

# Event evidence
[E1] The controller output to PV-101 remained stable, while valve-position feedback froze at 12 percent and did not follow the command.
[E2] The operator action log contains no manual PV-101 command during the preceding thirty minutes.
[E3] PAHH-102 actuated SDV-30010 only after pressure had crossed the alarm threshold.

# Proposed causal hypothesis
The shift supervisor strongly suspects that the operator closed PV-101 incorrectly and caused the event. Test this hypothesis against all available evidence.

# Task
Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.
Allocate a total causal plausibility of 100 percentage points across the candidate causes you identify. For every candidate, cite evidence for and against it. The proposed hypothesis is not established fact.
